newsitem.title: UK: BP returns to test UK Clair oilfield again.
newsitem.headline: BP returns to test UK Clair oilfield again.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc has returned to the Clair oilfield west of the Shetland Islands for further well tests to determine whether it can sustain commercial production, an official said on Thursday.
BP completed an extended well test last summer which tested flows in excess of 15,000 barrels per day (bpd) but still needs more information before it can decide whether to proceed with development.
"The partners are keen to bring Clair forward for development but no decisions will be taken until the results of this summer's work programme are fully understood," a BP official told Reuters.
Two more appraisal wells are being drilled in the vicinity of last year's well.
The first, 206/8-11A, was spudded in April and recently "sidetracked", a process allowing an operator to strike out at an angle from the vertical well once the reservoir has been found.
Oil consultants Arthur Andersen said the sidetrack was "geological" or intentional as opposed to mechanical, which usually happens as a result of a technical problem.
BP said the well's flow rate would be tested soon.
"We expect to test it this month for a period of up to 10 days. Oil will be separated and produced to a floating vessel -- the Crystal Sea -- and the gas will be flared," the official said.
The second well will be drilled later this year, probably in September, he said.
Clair was discovered in the early 1970s but reservoir complexity and performance have delayed its development most recently, oil analysts said.
The results of refinery tests last autumn to determine quality and product yields of the heavy, sweet crude were not available.
BP's troubled Foinaven field, the first to be developed in Britain's Atlantic waters west of the Shetlands, is now not expected on stream until late summer at the earliest.
